newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hog prices flat-up $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hog prices flat-up $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by firm packer demand and relatively light hog movement, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $46.50 to $47.50 in the country and $47.50 to $48.50 at the plant, sources there said.

Illinois hogs sold steady to up $0.50 at $47.00 to $48.00 in the country and up to $48.50 at plants. Indiana buyers said sales were steady at $46.00 to $47.00 in the country and $47.00 to $48.00, with a few at $48.50 at plants.
Some of the light hog movement this week was tied to talk that producers were slowing marketings as they resisted recent price declines.
However, price gains on Monday and projections for higher values Tuesday could encourage producers to market a few extra hogs, the dealers said.
Cash hog price gains were muted by another decline Monday in pork prices, they said.
Estimated gross cutout values Monday of a 175 lb hog carcass based on USDA cutting tests and carlot prices were down $0.72 to $0.83 per cwt.
